## 1. OBJECTIVE

## 2. IN SCOPE
- Determine the authenticated GitHub user via `gh api user --jq .login`.
- Create a new private repository named `bench-shs-multi` using `gh repo create` (or equivalent API call) under the authenticated account.
- Add the new repository as a remote named `origin` (or appropriate name) to the local git repository.
- Push every local branch to the new remote using a single command (e.g., `git push --all -u origin`).
- Parse `calc.py` to identify every public function (functions whose name does not start with `_`).
- For each public function, extract its one-line docstring (the first line of the docstring, stripped of surrounding whitespace).
- Open a new issue titled exactly `Benchmark audit` in the new repository using `gh issue create`.
- The issue body must list every public function in `calc.py` with its one-line docstring, formatted as a readable list (e.g., `- \`func_name(args)\` — docstring text`).
- Report the final repository URL (e.g., `https://github.com/<owner>/bench-shs-multi`) and the issue number to the user.

## 3. OUT OF SCOPE
- Modifying, refactoring, or reformatting `calc.py` or any other source file.

- Configuring branch protection rules, webhooks, GitHub Actions, or CI/CD.
- Creating labels, milestones, projects, or releases.
- Migrating issues, pull requests, or wiki content from any other repository.
- Pushing tags (only branches are in scope; tags may be pushed only if they are part of "all local branches" semantics — see Technical Constraints).
- Authenticating or re-authenticating `gh`; the tool is assumed already authenticated.
- Creating a local git repository; one is assumed to already exist in the working directory.
- Editing the issue after creation (no follow-up comments or edits unless required for correctness).
